precepts.text: Be not ashamed to confess thy sins, and force not the course of the river. The river is flowing, and you are trying to reroute it away from you. You are trying to dodge correction.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.text: Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to foolish men.
precepts.point: Some elders from other camps say that Moses left the truth. It says right there in verse 17, only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the people answered him: “According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They hearkened to Moses because they believed he was the man of the Lord. Moses led the people with integrity and character, even while judging Israel in the wilderness, and he kept that integrity all the way.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing, and they learned integrity and good character by being under a man the Lord was with. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

precepts.text: A captain's precept. Be as a father to the fatherless and instead of an husband unto thy mother, so shalt thou be as the son of the Most High. The whoremonger asks what he can do to this sister; the son of the Most High asks how to build up the young man.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

precepts.text: Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Who is this wisdom we are to seek? Christ is also known as wisdom: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

So when Sirach speaks of wisdom exalting her children, and when Proverbs has wisdom saying “By me princes rule”, it is Christ speaking. The Lord is the one who sets up all the kings and all the princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God by whom they rule.

To seek wisdom is to seek Christ. Those who seek him are the ones wisdom lays hold of, and the children she exalts are the ones he calls: the called, both Jews and Greeks.

precepts.text: By me princes rule; I love them that love me; those that seek me early shall find me; riches and honour are with me, yea, durable riches and righteousness. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
How do we seek wisdom? Wisdom answers in Proverbs: “By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.” The Lord sets up all the kings and princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you. “and those that seek me early shall find me.” We have a chance right now, in the midst of these wars and rumours of wars: we have to seek the Lord early, right now.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” Riches and honour are with Christ. Durable riches are not temporal, not temporary; they last a long time, forever, eternal. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”

That is how wisdom exalts her children and lays hold of them that seek her: she loves those who love her, she is found by those who seek her early, and she gives them lasting riches and righteousness.

precepts.text: Solomon loved the Lord and asked for an understanding heart to discern between good and bad; the speech pleased the Lord, who gave him a wise heart like none before or after, and also riches and honour he had not asked for.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
We have to be like Solomon: we have to pray for wisdom so that we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”, and at Gibeon “the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.”

Solomon answered, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, set in the midst of “a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.” “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”. As a youth, Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom.

“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” Because he “hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies”, God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.” And more: “I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave Solomon things he did not ask for because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek ye first the kingdom of heaven and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of Solomon’s book: wisdom exalted him because he sought her.

precepts.text: I prayed and understanding was given me; I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, esteemed riches nothing in comparison, loved her above health and beauty; all good things came to me with her, and I did not hide her riches.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Solomon tells it himself: “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.”

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” So the question is: do you prefer God’s wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires? “all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” Solomon did not care about anything else except wisdom.

“All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”. Wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He did not hide his wisdom. Sirach says the same: “refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Just as Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures. Searching after wisdom is a good thing; that is what we are supposed to do. That is how we should talk, it should be on our minds at all times, and everything should always go back to the scriptures.

precepts.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, but let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. Sirach 4:17-18: at first wisdom walks with him by crooked ways, brings fear and dread, torments him with her discipline until she may trust his soul, then returns the straight way, comforts him, and shows him her secrets. There is no cap on wisdom. Hebrews 11:6, without faith it is impossible to please him, and Romans 10:17, faith cometh by hearing the word of God, so increase your study.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If we lack wisdom, go to the source: go to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.

Sirach shows how wisdom deals with the one who seeks her: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” When we come into this truth we are not right, so wisdom walks with us in our crooked ways, and the Lord will jack us up because we are not doing it right; but wisdom will still be there. “Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There is no cap on wisdom.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That is the key: you have to believe. “But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we must build our faith. And “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” We have to increase our study as we see the days approaching, and continue to converse in the scriptures.

precepts.text: As a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. Isaiah 49:25, I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. Zechariah 3:8-9, my servant the Branch, Christ, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. Revelation 12:10-11, they overcame the accuser by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their lives unto the death.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him. They are wisdom’s children.

Isaiah shows what that pity does: “for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The Lord will fight those who fought against us, and he will save our children, because wisdom exalts her children.

He does it through Christ: “behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH”, and “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That is what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

And the end of it is in Revelation: “the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, and “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome by the blood of the Lamb; we must have faith and continue to be faithful, loving righteousness more than iniquity. The Father pities his children who fear him, and exalts them.

precepts.text: However close or trusted the person, accept no person against thy soul; your salvation is at stake.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.” The people named here are the closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you: thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, the friend which is as thine own soul. However close or trusted the person, accept no person against thy soul; your salvation is at stake.

Trust in a person is no cover for your soul. When someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. That is why the law says “neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare”: the reverence you have for a man cannot be allowed to cause thee to fall. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown.

precepts.text: Saul was tried by the laws of the Most High and went wrong; had he passed the test he would have been elevated, but wisdom forsook him and gave him over to his own ruin.
precepts.point: Why did the spirit leave Saul? Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first and tries him by her laws. Saul was put through a trial, whether he would keep the commandment given through the mouth of the prophet, and he went wrong; so the spirit forsook him and he was given over to his own ruin, that abyss of jealousy, envy, and hatred.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.” It was evident. Whatever Saul was doing and saying, his servants could tell an evil spirit was on him.

Why did the spirit leave Saul? Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first and tries him by her laws: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws. Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets. But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.”

Saul was put through a trial, whether he would keep the commandment given through the mouth of the prophet, and he went wrong. Had he passed the test he would have been elevated, but wisdom forsook him and gave him over to his own ruin, that abyss of jealousy, envy and hatred.

precepts.point: The old prophet claims an angel spoke to him by the word of the Most High telling him to bring the man back, but the scripture plainly states he lied. The man of God, giving reverence to the older prophet, goes back and eats.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.”

The man of God had his charge: “Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.” He repeated it to the old prophet of Bethel who rode after him and found him “sitting under an oak”. But the old prophet said, “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water.” The scripture plainly states it: “But he lied unto him.”

The man of God gave reverence to the older prophet, and “he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.” He let the reverence of a man cause him to fall.

precepts.text: Wisdom exalteth her children and layeth hold of them that seek her; especially with the new, the Most High deals with each differently and gives time to get it right.
precepts.point: Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Those who seek wisdom, she lays hold of and lifts up.

Especially with the new, the Most High deals with each one differently and gives time to get it right. Wisdom is not taken from a man the first time he stumbles. Ahab was not one who sought her; he held on to his sin, followed Baalim, and let Jezebel feed the prophets of Baal and the prophets of the groves at her table without ever checking her.

precepts.text: Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first, tormenting him in his mind until he rids his body of sin; if he goes wrong she forsakes him and gives him over to his own ruin, which is what happened to Ahab.
precepts.point: Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” Wisdom torments a man in his mind at the first, until he rids his body of sin.

“Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” That is for the one who comes through the trying.

“But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.” That is what happened to Ahab. He went wrong, wisdom forsook him, and he was given over to his own ruin: blaming Elijah for troubling Israel while he and his father’s house had forsaken the commandments, and letting Jezebel feed eight hundred and fifty false prophets at her table.

precepts.text: Do not always be the give-me person who then vanishes when it is time to give back.
precepts.point: The wicked borrows and pays not again, but the righteous shows mercy and gives. That is those people who borrow and then shut their hand when it comes time to pay. That is not the way we are supposed to be as a people.

note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous sheweth mercy, and giveth.” Ecclesiasticus puts it plainly: “Let not thine hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when thou shouldest repay.” That is those people who borrow and then shut their hand when it comes time to pay, the give-me person who vanishes when it is time to give back. That is not the way we are supposed to be as a people.

You cannot make it in this captivity alone. Everything we have, we have to share with one another. Black Wall Street is here; the little we have, we try to make sure our brothers and sisters are taken care of. The righteous “is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed.”

“I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.” The Most High never saw the righteous begging bread, because we are supposed to have each other; if we have each other we will not be begging bread, and we will be good in times of famine.

Good men, whose steps are ordered by the Most High, are men that keep the commandments. Somebody may say the Bible says none is good, which is true, but you have to fight to be good; Christ says strive to enter in through the straight gate. Wickedness will come and you may fall, but like Proverbs says, a righteous man falls seven times and gets back up again. “Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the Lord upholdeth him with his hand.” If you fall short of the glory and stay short, that is on you; get back up and reach for the full glory.

precepts.text: Do not turn your face or eye from the afflicted and needy, lest they curse you and be heard.
precepts.point: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves, but when they perish the righteous increase.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.” Ecclesiasticus says the same: “Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away thy face from a poor man. Turn not away thine eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse thee”.

Do not turn your face or your eye from the afflicted and the needy, for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer is heard. That is the many a curse that comes on the man who hides his eyes.

Sirach 12 says if you do good, know to whom you do it, and the law commands us to help our brothers who keep the commandments. Give to the poor among your brothers and you shall not lack; hide your eyes and the curse is heard.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown. Some of you men and women come into this truth and get offended, at the leadership, at some law that came out that you didn't like, or at another brother or sister, and you refuse to apply the scriptures and you leave this truth, all because you are angry at this person over yonder. Start with the leadership first. “Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.” Let not the reverence or love for any man cause thee to fall. That is very heavy right there. Sometimes we get in a situation where you love a man, a brother or sister, so much that you allow them to lead you into sin.

Tyler Perry has a wicked movie out called Ruthless; this thing is wicked as hell. There is a man set up as the highest, and a lady named Ruth loves him so much. He says, I need to cleanse you, and brings her in with seven men butt naked around the bed. He says, Ruth, do you love me? That is always the preface for some evil behind it: remember that dude Uzziah from Austin, he called every school, do you love me, do you love Jamal? She says yes, I love you. He says lay down, you must be seeded by the seven rings. She says, but I thought I was going to lay with you. He says no, I'm pure, you cannot lay with me, meanwhile he banged all seven dudes already. This movie is the devil, wicked as hell. The point is, the Bible says let not your reverence for man cause you to fall: she loved this guy so much she was willing to have these seven dudes gang-rape her. And we have seen that in some Israelite camps. When we were in Jamaica a sister came to us and said a particular camp came to Jamaica, impregnated the majority of the women and bounced back to America; what can we do? You better praise the Lord, it's out of my hands. You allow these people, who give themselves these flattering titles, I am the great Poobah, obey thou me, spread thou thy legs, and you go okay, you simple woman; and you brothers see that evil and don't say nothing. That is why Christ said let not your reverence for any man cause thee to fall. And guess what their colours are in that movie: purple. Everybody wearing purple. The SPLC, the media, have their hands in Hollywood: let's portray this evil cult that rapes men and women and murders people and drug-traffics and sells weapons and child-traffics, and give them purple, a purple cult. You cannot make this up. The whole world is against the prophets of God.

Sometimes you love somebody so much you are going to do whatever he or she says, and they will cause you to fall. Meaning what? Lose your crown.

moments.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Be not as a lion in thy house, nor frantick among thy servants. Especially if you are a weakling in the streets: out camping, sin walks right by, and you are afraid to go into the scriptures and call it out. Then you go in the house and roar.

note.label: This Woman's Work

points: Here is the number one thing that helped the teacher overcome that spirit. For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways: the she is wisdom, the Holy Spirit. When you first come into this truth, you are still meddling with your sins, and wisdom still walks with you; you are still in here learning. That is the voice that keeps telling you, what are you doing, the Lord is going to judge you.

And bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws. That is the secret: fear. Bad things happen to you to correct you, because whom the Lord loves he chastens. You might have been in your sin and something happened, and you know why it happened. In life, ask yourself two questions about everything that happens: why did it happen, and what is God trying to teach me?

The reason a lot of you are not going to stop is that you have no fear. It is pleasurable. But when you understand that God is going to judge you, and that he will correct you, you leave it alone, the same way a child does not go against the parent's order because the child knows correction is coming.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

points: Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets. When wisdom can trust your soul, you are comforted, and that is when you start understanding the secrets of the Bible.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

points: For there is a shame that bringeth sin; and there is a shame which is glory and grace. Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.

You cannot allow the reverence of anybody to cause you to fall. You have reverence for a person, and that person bugs out and says, I am out; he went through his trials and he failed. So because he failed when he was tested by the Lord, now you leave too, because you like him? You are supposed to be in this truth because you love the Lord.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: This is for you women in this truth that are single mothers, not by choice or because you didn't know the truth. I'm not tearing you down; I was tearing down the strong independent woman that says, I don't need no man, I can raise these kids by myself.

Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother: so shalt thou be as the son of the most High. The righteous men in this truth are thinking like this: be role models to the children that don't have a man of God in their life. Let the men groom your children so they'll be successful serving God and won't be a statistic. Don't just think, I need to find a baby daddy; if it happens, fine, but that should not be the first thing on your mind. And you men should not be trying to take advantage of the women that are single mothers.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Wisdom exalteth her children and layeth hold of them that seek her. Christ is the wisdom of God, 1 Corinthians 1:24, and Proverbs 8:16-19 says by me princes rule, I love them that love me, those that seek me early shall find me, and riches and honour are with me, durable riches that last forever. Seek him early now in the midst of wars and rumours of wars.

Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

points: “Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother”. Older men, some young men have no father in this truth. Be their father, their mentor, give direction and spark this in them. You're not trying to bag the mom. Make sure the next generation has these scriptures. Without a father these young men will be led astray. Keep guiding and molding them until they reach that age. Young people, I'm proud of you. Stay faithful, stay godly, and let's take this kingdom.
